The Senate Committee on Legislative Compliance has thrown its weight behind the Federal Character Commission’s decision to institute legal proceedings against the Nigeria Customs Service over alleged violations of the federal character principle in its 2025/2026 recruitment exercise. The committee also urged the commission to extend its scrutiny to other ministries, departments and agencies of the Federal Government to ensure compliance with the Federal Character Commission Act. The committee made its position known in a letter dated November 18, 2026, signed by its Chairman, Senator Garba Madoki, and addressed to the Chairman of the Federal Character Commission, and titled, ‘Commendation on the Federal Character Commission’s Action Against the Nigeria Customs Service for Non-Compliance with the Federal Character Principle in its Recruitment Exercise’. In the letter, the committee commended the commission for taking legal action against the Customs Service over alleged non-compliance with the provisions of the Federal Character Commission Act. “I write to commend the Federal Character Commission for its bold decision to institute legal proceedings against the Nigeria Customs Service over alleged non-compliance with the provisions of the Federal Character Commission Act in its 2025/2026 recruitment process,” the letter stated. NAFDAC intercepts unregistered beverages, skin-lightening injections at Kano airport Customs target faster cargo clearance Onne CAC charges officers to plug revenue leakages “It is particularly encouraging that the Commission has taken concrete steps to enforce compliance with its statutory mandate, rather than allowing apparent violations of the Federal Character principle to go unchallenged,” it said. The committee further assured the Commission of its support, citing its oversight responsibility to ensure compliance with legislation, resolutions and directives of the Senate. “In view of the Committee’s oversight mandate, particularly as it relates to ensuring compliance with legislation, resolutions and directives of the Senate, the Committee wishes to assure the Commission of its full support in this important endeavour,” the letter added. It also urged the commission to extend similar scrutiny to other government institutions where there might be violations of the Act, particularly in recruitment, appointments and other personnel-related processes. “While commending the Commission for this initiative, the Committee wishes to encourage it to extend similar scrutiny to other Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) of the Federal Government where there may be instances of non-compliance with the provisions of the Federal Character Commission Act, particularly in their recruitment, appointments and other personnel-related processes,” it stated. According to the committee, such action would strengthen enforcement of the law and ensure that no government agency is exempted from the principles of fairness and equitable representation.
